newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK insurers' 9-mth profits under pressure.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK insurers' 9-mth profits under pressure.

text.p: The prolonged weakness in UK private motor insurance rates and hurricanes in North America are likely to keep nine month profits for UK insurers Commercial Union and General Accident under pressure.
Nine month pre-tax profits for Commercial Union are forecast at 335 to 355 million stg and for General Accident at 300 to 324 million stg, analysts said.

Despite reports from some direct motor insurers that UK personal motor rates have seen steady if modest gains over the last few months, much of this year has been notable only for its stability for many insurers in the motor market.
The 25 percent decline in rates over the last two years appears to have bottomed out, but analysts are cautious of predicting across-the-board increases in the near future.

"Insurers require price rises of at least five percent in order to offset the rise in claims costs," said analysts at Merrill Lynch in a recent research note. "Anything less than that implies that underwriting results are still deteriorating." Merrill Lynch expects CU's worldwide underwriting result to fall to a 223 million stg loss from 118 million last year, while GA's could decline to 158 million stg from 62 million.
The deterioration will come mainly from the UK and United States, where in CU's case particularly, the hurricane season could have had "a material impact".
Life assurance profits, however, are forecast to rise. CU has already reported a 23 percent increase in new life business for the first nine months to 2.215 billion stg.
Its continental European operations underpinned this performance, with France reporting a big jump in premiums.
